## holst

```text
Usage: holst [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...

  Drive the Holst (holst.so) collaborative whiteboard from the command line.

Options:
  --json           Emit machine-readable JSON.
  --select TEXT    Keep only these dotted fields (comma separated or repeated)
                   of the JSON result, like boards.id. Implies --json.
  --out FILE       Write the JSON result to this file and print only a short
                   summary. Implies --json.
  --base-url TEXT  Holst host (for on-premise installs).
  --version        Show the version and exit.
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  auth        Manage the personal access token used to reach Holst.
  backup      Download board snapshots (the "version history" of a board).
  board       Create, inspect, and manage boards.
  completion  Print the shell completion script for SHELL.
  content     Read and write the objects on a board.
  doctor      Check the setup: versions, paths, credentials, Node, yjs...
  mcp         Serve Holst boards to an AI agent over MCP (stdio).
  repl        Start the interactive session (default when no subcommand...
  session     Inspect and reset the persistent CLI session.
  skill       The agent skill file that ships with this CLI.
  template    Browse board templates.
  workspace   List workspaces, inspect members, and select the active one.
```

## holst auth

```text
Usage: holst auth [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage the personal access token used to reach Holst.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  diagnose   Work out why authentication is failing, without revealing...
  login      Store a session token, or obtain one with email and password.
  logout     Remove the stored token.
  methods    Show which sign-in methods an email address can use.
  pair       Pair this CLI with your Holst account the way the desktop...
  redeem     Redeem a granted pairing code for a session token.
  send-code  Ask Holst to mail a one-time password.
  sessions   List active sessions on the account.
  status     Show credential configuration; --verify checks it against...
  token      Manage personal access tokens (scope: organization audit...
  whoami     Show the authenticated Holst account.
```

## holst auth diagnose

```text
Usage: holst auth diagnose [OPTIONS]

  Work out why authentication is failing, without revealing credentials.

  Signs in (or uses the stored credential), then tries each known way of
  presenting it to /gapi/current_user and reports the HTTP status of each.

Options:
  -e, --email TEXT  Sign in first with this address.
  --password TEXT   Password for --email (prompted if omitted).
  -h, --help        Show this message and exit.
```

## holst auth login

```text
Usage: holst auth login [OPTIONS]

  Store a session token, or obtain one with email and password.

  A personal access token from the Holst UI will NOT work here: it only grants
  the organization audit-events scope. Use `auth pair`, --email, or copy the
  session token your browser holds.

Options:
  -t, --token TEXT  Session token (from the browser or `auth pair`).
  --cookie TEXT     Session cookie copied from the browser, e.g. 'name=value;
                    name2=value2'.
  -e, --email TEXT  Sign in with email and password instead.
  --password TEXT   Password for --email. Omitted, it is prompted for without
                    echo.
  --password-stdin  Read the password from standard input (keeps it out of
                    shell history).
  --send-code       With --email: have Holst mail a one-time password first.
  --no-verify       Store without contacting the server.
  -h, --help        Show this message and exit.
```

## holst auth logout

```text
Usage: holst auth logout [OPTIONS]

Options:

```

## holst auth methods

```text
Usage: holst auth methods [OPTIONS]

  Show which sign-in methods an email address can use.

  Run this first when a login fails: many Holst accounts have no permanent
  password and accept only a one-time code or OAuth.

Options:
  -e, --email TEXT  Address to check.  [required]
  -h, --help        Show this message and exit.
```

## holst auth token

```text
Usage: holst auth token [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage personal access tokens (scope: organization audit events only).

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  create  Create a personal access token; the secret is shown only once.
  list    List personal access tokens.
  revoke  Revoke a personal access token.
```

## holst auth token create

```text
Usage: holst auth token create [OPTIONS]

  Create a personal access token; the secret is shown only once.

Options:
  -n, --name TEXT    Human-readable token name.  [required]
  --scope TEXT       Scope to grant (repeatable).  [default:
                     organization:audit_events_read]
  --expires-at TEXT  Expiry timestamp (ISO 8601).
  -h, --help         Show this message and exit.
```

## holst board

```text
Usage: holst board [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Create, inspect, and manage boards.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  comments   List comment threads on a board (metadata; text lives in the...
  create     Create a board.
  delete     Move a board to trash, or delete it permanently.
  duplicate  Duplicate a board.
  favorites  List, add, or remove favorite boards.
  info       Show a board (defaults to the selected one).
  list       List boards in a workspace.
  members    List users with explicit access to a board.
  recent     List recently opened boards.
  rename     Rename a board.
  restore    Restore a board from the workspace trash.
  share      Show or update link-sharing settings.
  trash      List boards in the workspace trash.
  url        Print the web URL of a board.
  use        Select the active board for later commands.
```

## holst completion

```text
Usage: holst completion [OPTIONS] {bash|zsh|fish}

  Print the shell completion script for SHELL.

    bash:  holst completion bash >> ~/.bashrc
    zsh:   holst completion zsh  >> ~/.zshrc

Options:
```

## holst content

```text
Usage: holst content [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Read and write the objects on a board.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  add-arrow    Connect two points, or two objects, with an arrow.
  add-card     Put a card on a board: a document block that grows with...
  add-frame    Put a frame on a board.
  add-shape    Put a shape on a board: a box, a flowchart step, a BPMN...
  add-sticker  Put a sticky note on a board.
  add-text     Put a text block on a board.
  apply        Add, change and remove many objects in one transaction.
  delete       Remove objects from a board.
  objects      List the objects on a board.
  raw          Dump the decoded CRDT tree as JSON.
  shapes       List the shape kinds `add-shape --kind` accepts.
  summary      Summarise a board: object counts by type.
  text         Dump every readable string on a board, one per line.
  update       Change an object that is already on a board.
```

## holst content add-arrow

```text
Usage: holst content add-arrow [OPTIONS]

  Connect two points, or two objects, with an arrow.

Options:
  --board TEXT                    Board to write to.
  --from-object TEXT              Id of the object to start at.
  --to-object TEXT                Id of the object to end at.
  --from-x FLOAT                  Start point x, when not attached.
  --from-y FLOAT                  Start point y, when not attached.
  --to-x FLOAT                    End point x, when not attached.
  --to-y FLOAT                    End point y, when not attached.
  --type [straight|elbow|curved]  How the line is routed.  [default: elbow]
  --color TEXT                    Line colour.
  --stroke-width FLOAT            Line thickness, in points.
  --head-start [none|figma|miro|arc|triangle-filled|triangle|circle-filled|circle|rhombus-filled|rhombus|stick|stick-stick|triadius|triadius-stick|triadius-circle|stick-circle|slash]
                                  Arrowhead at the start.
  --head-end [none|figma|miro|arc|triangle-filled|triangle|circle-filled|circle|rhombus-filled|rhombus|stick|stick-stick|triadius|triadius-stick|triadius-circle|stick-circle|slash]
                                  Arrowhead at the end.
  --frame TEXT                    Id of the frame to place this inside.
                                  Coordinates stay absolute.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content add-card

```text
Usage: holst content add-card [OPTIONS]

  Put a card on a board: a document block that grows with its text.

Options:
  --board TEXT     Board to write to.
  --x FLOAT        Board x coordinate.  [default: 0.0]
  --y FLOAT        Board y coordinate.  [default: 0.0]
  --color TEXT     Palette token such as yellow4, or a hex value.
  --frame TEXT     Id of the frame to place this inside. Coordinates stay
                   absolute.
  -t, --text TEXT  Card body.
  --width FLOAT    Width, in points. Height follows the text.
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content add-frame

```text
Usage: holst content add-frame [OPTIONS]

  Put a frame on a board.

Options:
  --board TEXT                    Board to write to.
  --x FLOAT                       Board x coordinate.  [default: 0.0]
  --y FLOAT                       Board y coordinate.  [default: 0.0]
  --color TEXT                    Palette token such as yellow4, or a hex
                                  value.
  --frame TEXT                    Id of the frame to place this inside.
                                  Coordinates stay absolute.

                                  --height are given.  [default: 16:9]
  -n, --name TEXT                 Frame label.
  --width FLOAT                   Custom width, in points.
  --height FLOAT                  Custom height, in points.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content add-shape

```text
Usage: holst content add-shape [OPTIONS]

  Put a shape on a board: a box, a flowchart step, a BPMN symbol.

  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content apply

```text
Usage: holst content apply [OPTIONS]

  Add, change and remove many objects in one transaction.

Options:
  --board TEXT     Board to write to.
  -f, --file PATH  JSON list of operations, or {"objects": [...]}. An entry
                   with no "op" creates an object of its "type" (frame,
                   sticker, text, shape, card, arrow) and its remaining keys
                   match that add-* command's options; "op": "update" or
                   "delete" names an existing "id".  [required]
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content delete

```text
Usage: holst content delete [OPTIONS]

  Remove objects from a board.

  A frame takes its contents with it, as it does in Holst; --keep-children
  leaves them behind at the top level. This cannot be undone from the CLI --
  the board's own undo history belongs to the browser session that made the
  change.

Options:
  --board TEXT                 Board to write from.
  --object TEXT                Id of an object to remove. Repeatable.
                               [required]
  --keep-children / --cascade  Whether the contents of a deleted frame stay on
                               the board.  [default: cascade]
  -y, --yes                    Skip the confirmation prompt.
  -h, --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content objects

```text
Usage: holst content objects [OPTIONS]

  List the objects on a board.

Options:
  --board TEXT                 Board to read.
  --snapshot PATH              Decode a local snapshot file instead.
  --key TEXT                   Snapshot key (implies --snapshot-only; defaults
                               to the newest).
  --snapshot-only              Read the newest snapshot instead of joining the
                               live board.
  --provider [hocuspocus|hud]  Snapshot encoding. Detected from the board when
                               omitted.
  --type TEXT                  Only objects of this type.
  -n, --limit INTEGER          Maximum objects to show.  [default: 50]
  -h, --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

```text
  Dump every readable string on a board, one per line.

Options:
  --board TEXT                 Board to read.
  --snapshot PATH              Decode a local snapshot file instead.
  --key TEXT                   Snapshot key (implies --snapshot-only; defaults
                               to the newest).
  --snapshot-only              Read the newest snapshot instead of joining the
                               live board.
  --provider [hocuspocus|hud]  Snapshot encoding. Detected from the board when
                               omitted.
  -h, --help                   Show this message and exit.
```

## holst content update

```text
Usage: holst content update [OPTIONS]

  Change an object that is already on a board.

Options:
  --board TEXT     Board to write to.
  --object TEXT    Id of the object to change.  [required]
  --x FLOAT        New board x coordinate.
  --y FLOAT        New board y coordinate.
  --width FLOAT    New width, in points.
  --height FLOAT   New height, in points.
  --color TEXT     New colour: a palette token, or a hex value.
  -t, --text TEXT  Replace the object's text.
  -n, --name TEXT  Replace a frame's label.
  --frame TEXT     Move into this frame. Pass "none" to take it out of one.
  --to-front       Put it above everything else.
  --to-back        Put it below everything else.
  -h, --help       Show this message and exit.
```

## holst doctor

```text
Usage: holst doctor [OPTIONS]

  Check the setup: versions, paths, credentials, Node, yjs and the API.

  Exits 1 when any check fails; warnings do not change the exit code.

Options:
  --offline                Skip the checks that need the network (api, auth).
  --timeout INTEGER RANGE  Seconds to wait for each network check.  [default:
                           10; x>=1]
  -h, --help               Show this message and exit.
```

## holst mcp

```text
Usage: holst mcp [OPTIONS]

  Serve Holst boards to an AI agent over MCP (stdio).

  The server speaks the Model Context Protocol on stdin and stdout. Root flags
  go before the command, --read-only after it:

    holst --base-url https://holst.example mcp --read-only

  Client setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and Codex is in the
  README, section "MCP server".

Options:
  --read-only  Hide the tools that create or change boards and objects.
  -h, --help   Show this message and exit.
```

## holst skill install

```text
Usage: holst skill install [OPTIONS]

  Install SKILL.md where your coding agent looks for skills.

  Without -a and -g/--project you are asked; -y takes universal in this
  directory. With --json nothing is asked: pass -a and -g/--project, or -y.

Options:
  -a, --agent [claude-code|codex|copilot|cursor|gemini|universal]
                                  Agent to install for; repeatable. Omit to be
                                  asked.
  -g, --global                    Install for the current user instead of this
                                  directory.
  --project                       Install into the current directory. The
                                  default when asked.
  --dir DIRECTORY                 Explicit directory; bypasses the agent
                                  layout and makes no links.
  -y, --yes                       Do not prompt; take the defaults.
  -h, --help                      Show this message and exit.
```
